core_claim: The brain combines information across sensory modalities (visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory) through space-time binding. Congruent multisensory input enhances processing efficiency and comfort; incongruence creates confusion and effort.

falsification_criteria: Spatially/temporally congruent multisensory input does not speed reaction times or enhance perception compared to unimodal control
Incongruent (conflicting) multisensory input does not increase reaction time or error rates
Blocking one sensory modality (e.g., vision) does not impair interpretation of congruent input in another modality (e.g., auditory)
scope_boundaries: Applies to sensory integration across all modalities; most evidence from vision-audition
Does NOT explain pure unimodal perception or attention
Scope LIMITED to animals with multiple sensory systems; subcortical (superior colliculus) mechanisms may differ from cortical

environmental_predictions.statement: Environments with spatially/temporally congruent multisensory cues (e.g., footsteps synchronized with visual motion) produce faster stimulus detection and enhanced sense of presence compared to incongruent or unimodal cues
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Multisensory neurons in superior colliculus and cortex integrate congruent signals via space-time binding rules. Superadditive response (enhanced compared to sum of unimodal responses) speeds perception and action.

competing_predictions.prediction: Congruence benefit comes from reduced prediction error, not multisensory superadditivity per se

environmental_predictions.statement: Acoustically incongruent architectural spaces (e.g., auditory reverberation mismatched to visual room size) increase cognitive load and discomfort even when individual sensory signals are acceptable
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Multisensory conflict creates binding uncertainty. Neurons can't reliably determine whether signals are from same source or different sources. Conflict resolution requires effortful attention.

environmental_predictions.statement: Architectural environments that support natural audio-visual correspondence (e.g., intimate scale allows hearing conversations at seen distances) produce enhanced sense of place and social connection
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Congruent audio-visual space-time binding creates unified scene representation. Poor correspondence (hearing loud noise from invisible source, or seeing speech without proportional sound) fragments environmental coherence.

competing_predictions.prediction: Place sense depends on allocentric mapping, not on audio-visual binding

characteristic_questions: What sensory modalities are present in this environment (visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory)?
Are cues from different modalities spatially and temporally congruent?
What is the scale match between visual space and acoustic space?
Are there crossmodal illusions or ventriloquism effects (e.g., sound pulling perception of visual location)?
What sensory dominance patterns are expected (vision typically dominant, but varies by context)?

panel_persona.voice: I evaluate environments through multisensory integration: Are the signals from different senses binding into a unified, efficient percept? Or are they conflicting, creating confusion and cognitive load?
typical_critiques: Reaction time improvements with multisensory input are robust, but alternative explanations exist (attentional orienting, not binding).
Measure integration directly (e.g., superadditivity indices, not just behavioral benefit).
Space-time binding rules vary across neurons and brain regions; be specific about level of analysis.
Individual differences in sensory dominance are large; expect noise in group-level predictions.
blind_spots: Multisensory integration research focuses heavily on vision-audition; olfactory-visual, tactile-visual integrations understudied
May overestimate benefit of congruence; humans often adapt to sensory mismatch
Limited account of how meaning (semantic congruence) versus space-time congruence affects integration
Does not explain why some incongruence is amusing (humor) rather than aversive (uncanny valley)
complementary_frameworks: predictive-processing (congruence reduces prediction error; incongruence increases it)
default-mode-dynamics (multisensory integration in DMN may support mental scene construction)
neuromodulatory-systems (attention-driven neuromodulation (dopamine, acetylcholine) enhances multisensory integration)

meta.notes: Neurophysiology highly robust. Behavioral predictions well-supported. Audio-visual incongruence in architecture understudied relative to visibility and spatial legibility.
